item.title: Serendipitous Discoveries from the Age of Charles I
item.description: "The results exemplify serendipity, defined as the fortunate but accidental discovery of valuable and illuminating information." David Cressy tells us about using a random number generator to create a serendipitous approach to the research for his new book, Careers and Crises in the Age of Charles I. The post Serendipitous Discoveries from the Age of Charles I appeared first on Boydell and Brewer.

item.title: 18th Century Women as Writers, Readers and Thinkers
item.description: The 18th century was an era of profound change. Enlightenment championed reason and logic, and advancements in technology sparked an industrial revolution. However, women were seen as inferior to men and were expected to have traditional domestic roles. In this blog, discover 6 books that explore how eighteenth-century women challenged societal expectations. The post 18th Century Women as Writers, Readers and Thinkers appeared first on Boydell and Brewer.

item.title: The Shaping of Global Narratives
item.description: In episode 3 of the new podcast, The Humanities in the World, Samantha Pinto and Nasser Rabbat examine how global narratives have often been shaped and repurposed to serve specific cultural and political agendas, and how historical figures and archaeological discoveries have been harnessed to propose specific visions of history and the world. The post The Shaping of Global Narratives appeared first on Boydell and Brewer.

item.title: 2025: 10 books you may have missed
item.description: Whether your interests lie in discovering the history of the violin or exploring how the European Middle Ages has been used in American culture, 2025 saw a wealth of new titles published. Here, we bring together 10 books from 2025 that you may have missed... The post 2025: 10 books you may have missed appeared first on Boydell and Brewer.

item.title: Books to look out for in January 2026
item.description: New year & new books! Explore the history of choral singing in Britain, discover the legacies of women journalists in Brazil, and uncover the hidden publishing networks in Restoration London. Explore January's new releases... The post Books to look out for in January 2026 appeared first on Boydell and Brewer.

item.title: Manasses of Hierges: Translating a Lost Voice
item.description: In this Q&A blog, Nicholas Paul and Wolfgang Mueller share their motivations and challenges behind translating a previously unknown medieval Latin text, and how this text gives a contrasting perspective on crusader life with William of Tyre’s chronicle. The post Manasses of Hierges: Translating a Lost Voice appeared first on Boydell and Brewer.

item.title: Nature’s Stage: Science, the Unknown and the Romance of it All
item.description: "In opera, the raw, untamed power of nature became a central character." Mark A. Pottinger explores how scientific discoveries and Romantic ideals intertwined in the art of opera during the early 1800s. The post Nature’s Stage: Science, the Unknown and the Romance of it All appeared first on Boydell and Brewer.

item.title: Echoes of Borrowing: Beowulf and Grettis Saga
item.description: Can the smallest of details in a story serve as a clue in a much larger historical puzzle? In this Q&A Richard North shares what inspired his love of the Old Norse language, explores new theories about Beowulf and Grettis saga, and reflects on why we continue to care so deeply about ancient stories—not just as isolated masterpieces, but as part of a fragile, interconnected world of lost cultures. The post Echoes of Borrowing: Beowulf and Grettis Saga appeared first on Boydell and Brewer.

item.title: Accused as a Witch: How Children Become Targets—and What Safeguarding Requires
item.description: What makes a witchcraft accusation against a child feel “true” enough for adults to act on it? Claire P. Ayelotan explores how this question led to the research for her book, Yoruba Pentecostalism and Child Witchcraft Accusations. The post Accused as a Witch: How Children Become Targets—and What Safeguarding Requires appeared first on Boydell and Brewer.
